description:
John Flavel’s life introduces a study of perseverance, pastoral care and the Christian response to suffering. Yang places the Puritan minister within the religious pressures of his time, then follows his continuing work through restrictions, displacement and personal bereavement. The account highlights his determination to preach, care for people and write for their spiritual benefit, even when ordinary opportunities for ministry were curtailed.

The presentation considers how Flavel’s private spiritual life shaped his public usefulness. Meditation, self-examination and assurance are linked with preaching that searched and comforted hearers. His writings continued to influence others beyond his own congregation and lifetime. The discussion also identifies humility, meekness and love as qualities that helped him pursue peace with fellow believers while remaining committed to his convictions.

Suffering is explored through the Puritan image of a school in which God teaches his children. Drawing on Flavel’s counsel about keeping the heart, the study urges believers to guard against abandoning Christ under pressure and to apply Scripture inwardly and outwardly. The closing discussion turns this historical example into a challenge to live wholeheartedly for Christ, seeking his honour through faithful obedience in the circumstances God gives.

questions.question: Why does the presentation begin with Flavel’s historical setting?
questions.answer: The background helps explain the restrictions under which he ministered. The account describes religious conformity, the removal of ministers from their churches and further limits on where they could live and meet. These circumstances give context to his continuing pastoral work and writing.

questions.question: How did Flavel continue serving when public ministry was restricted?
questions.answer: The account describes meetings in homes and outdoor places, pastoral contact maintained in difficult circumstances and a substantial writing ministry. These examples are used to show his determination to teach and care for people despite changing restrictions and personal risk.

questions.question: What connection is made between Flavel’s inner life and his preaching?
questions.answer: Yang links the effectiveness of his preaching with meditation, self-examination and his own spiritual experience. His ministry is presented as speaking truths that had affected his own heart. The account also emphasises careful explanation, searching application and comfort for troubled consciences.

questions.question: What does the image of a school of affliction mean in this study?
questions.answer: The Puritans are described as viewing suffering as a setting in which God graciously teaches his children. Flavel’s own bereavements and persecution give the presentation a personal context for that theme. The emphasis is on learning faithfulness to Christ in the midst of difficulty.

questions.question: What danger does Flavel’s counsel about keeping the heart address?
questions.answer: The selected counsel concerns the temptation to shrink back from Christ when suffering for his sake becomes costly. It calls believers to guard their hearts and consider the honour of the Redeemer. The study presents perseverance as an expression of valuing Christ and trusting his promises.

questions.question: How should believers respond practically to suffering?
questions.answer: The presentation recommends prayer and the inward and outward application of Scripture. It directs attention to the condition of the heart as well as outward circumstances. The closing discussion encourages continued worship and obedience, with Christ’s honour as the believer’s aim.

questions.question: Which personal qualities does Yang highlight in the discussion of Flavel?
questions.answer: When asked what distinguished him, Yang points to humility, meekness and love. He connects these qualities with a desire for unity despite disagreements and with the affection people had for Flavel’s ministry. These observations accompany the account of his preaching and writing gifts.

questions.question: What application does the closing discussion draw from studying the Puritans?
questions.answer: The closing speaker urges the church to share their hunger for Christ and Scripture and to express it in daily life. The goal presented is wholehearted faithfulness whether or not someone becomes historically well known. Listeners are encouraged to serve Christ in the circumstances they actually face.
